cards.title: Rating scale, notchChange and notchCalculator (src/ratings/notch.mjs)
cards.context:
WHY: REQ-06-02 (Should) asks for a notch calculator helper, and REQ-03-12 (Must, card T-02) needs the shared signed notch count. Build this module first. New file in an empty src/. Plain Node 18+ ESM .mjs, package.json type=module, script test=node --test. Do NOT add dependencies.

FILE: src/ratings/notch.mjs. Three named exports, imports nothing.

1) RATING_SCALE: exactly these 19 strings, best first: ["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"]. Minus is ASCII '-'. Object.freeze recommended (must still pass assert.deepStrictEqual against a plain array).

2) notchChange(previous, current) -> RATING_SCALE.indexOf(current) - RATING_SCALE.indexOf(previous). Positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged. (BBB,BBB-)=1, (BBB-,BB+)=1, (BBB,BB+)=2, (BBB+,BB+)=3, (AAA,CCC-)=18, (A,A)=0, (BB+,BBB-)=-1, (BB,BBB)=-3, (CCC-,AAA)=-18.

3) notchCalculator(previous, current) -> { notches, direction, wl }, exactly these 3 keys. notches === notchChange(...) (same sign); direction 'downgrade' if >0, 'upgrade' if <0, 'unchanged' if 0; wl (Ind. 13 rule): 0 if notches<=1 (incl. unchanged and every upgrade), 1 if ===2, 2 if >=3. NOTE: the POC doc example 'BBB+ -> BB+ = 2 notches, WL=1' is a known typo; business decided 3 notches, wl 2. This rule deliberately differs from Ind. 12 (T-02): do not share thresholds.

VALIDATION (binding): each argument must be strictly one of the 19 strings (typeof v === 'string' && RATING_SCALE.includes(v)); anything else throws RangeError (null, undefined, 42, {}, missing argument, 'bbb+', ' BBB+', 'BBB+ ', 'BBB\u2212', '', 'CC', 'C', 'D', 'NR', 'WD', 'Baa1'). Never String()/trim/toUpperCase, never default fallback. Message text is free but should name the bad argument. Validate both arguments in notchChange; notchCalculator may call notchChange. Any extra exported helper is extra API: keep minimal; T-02 must not need it.

PURITY: no node:fs, fetch, console, module-level mutable state.

UNIT TESTS: test/ratings/notch.test.mjs, node:test + node:assert/strict, TDD. Cover AC-1 (deepStrictEqual, 19 distinct), AC-2/3 examples, AC-4/8 INVALID list both positions + missing arg with assert.throws(fn, RangeError), AC-5/6 deepStrictEqual objects, AC-7 loop over all 361 pairs.

Commit messages: plain, '<card id>: <what changed>', no AI attribution.
acceptance: AC-1 [P0] — a wrong scale shifts every notch count and every WL built on it: Given `import { RATING_SCALE } from "../../src/ratings/notch.mjs"`, when it is read, then `assert.deepStrictEqual(RATING_SCALE, ["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"])`, `new Set(RATING_SCALE).size === 19`, `RATING_SCALE[0] === "AAA"`, `RATING_SCALE[18

AC-2 [P0] — a wrong count gives Ind. 12 a wrong WL for every client: Given two valid codes, when `notchChange(previous, current)` is called on a downgrade, then it returns the integer `RATING_SCALE.indexOf(current) - RATING_SCALE.indexOf(previous)`: ("BBB","BBB-") → 1; ("BBB-","BB+") → 1; ("BBB","BB+") → 2; ("BBB+","BB+") → 3; ("AAA","CCC-") → 18.

AC-3 [P0] — a wrong sign turns an upgrade into a downgrade: Given two valid codes, when `notchChange` is called on an unchanged or upgraded pair, then ("A","A") → 0; ("CCC-","CCC-") → 0; ("BB+","BBB-") → -1; ("BB","BBB") → -3; ("CCC-","AAA") → -18. Unchanged is `+0`, not `-0` (`assert.strictEqual` tells them apart).

AC-4 [P0] — bad input that returns a number silently hides a downgrade: Given each `v` in INVALID, when `notchChange(v, "BBB")` or `notchChange("BBB", v)` is called, then it throws `RangeError` and returns nothing. `notchChange("BBB")` (current missing) also throws `RangeError`.

AC-5 [P1] — the helper suggests a wrong WL, but the analyst can still count by hand (REQ-06-02 is Should): Given a downgrade, when `notchCalculator(previous, current)` is called, then it deep-strict-equals
AC-6 [P1] — an upgrade shown as a risk misleads the analyst, who has a workaround: Given an unchanged or upgraded pair, when `notchCalculator` is called, then it deep-strict-equals

AC-7 [P1] — a pair outside the examples gives a wrong helper result, with a workaround: Given every ordered pair (p, c) of the 361 pairs from `RATING_SCALE`, when `notchCalculator(p, c)` is called, then

AC-8 [P1] — the helper returns something for bad input, with a workaround: Given each `v` in INVALID, when `notchCalculator(v, "BBB")` or `notchCalculator("BBB", v)` is called, then it throws `RangeError`.

cards.title: Indicator 12 country rating change WL (src/indicators/countryRating.mjs)
cards.context:
WHY: REQ-03-12 (Must). Ind. 12 Country rating change gets its WL (0-4, higher worse) from the sovereign rating notch change; rule mirrors the Excel dropdown sheet exactly. Depends on T-01 which provides src/ratings/notch.mjs: RATING_SCALE (19 grades) and notchChange(previous,current) = signed integer, positive = downgrade, throws RangeError unless each argument is exactly one of the 19 codes (incl. null, undefined, 42, {}, missing args, wrong-case/padded strings).

FILE: src/indicators/countryRating.mjs. ONLY import: notchChange (RATING_SCALE only if needed) from '../ratings/notch.mjs'. No deps.

EXPORT: countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current) -> 0|1|2 (number). n = notchChange(previous,current); return 1 if n===1, 2 if n>=2, else 0 (unchanged and every upgrade -> 0). Examples: (BBB,BBB-)=1, (BBB-,BB+)=1, (BBB,BB+)=2, (BBB+,BB+)=2, (AAA,CCC-)=2, (AA,AA)=0, (BB+,BBB-)=0, (BB,BBB)=0, (CCC-,AAA)=0.
NOTE: deliberately different from notchCalculator's wl (Ind. 13 rule). Do NOT reuse notchCalculator; do not change notch.mjs.
Declare exactly two parameters, no defaults/rest/override parameter, so countryRatingChangeWl.length === 2. Computes only from its two arguments (caller passes the analyst-confirmed or edited rating); nothing cached between calls.

VALIDATION: delegate to notchChange so every invalid input throws RangeError, incl. countryRatingChangeWl() with no args. Never catch/swallow, coerce, trim, case-fold or default.

PURITY: no I/O, console, module-level state.
OUT OF SCOPE: fetching/pre-filling sovereign rating, 12-month window (REQ-02-02), Ind. 13, override flag, UI.

UNIT TESTS: test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs, node:test + node:assert/strict: AC-9 examples with assert.strictEqual; AC-10 loop over all 361 ordered pairs vs notchChange; AC-11 INVALID list both positions + no-arg call with assert.throws(fn, RangeError); AC-12 edit sequence and .length check.

Commit messages: plain, '<card id>: <what changed>', no AI attribution.
acceptance: AC-9 [P0] — a wrong Ind. 12 WL rates a client wrongly for compliance (the Must requirement): Given `import { countryRatingChangeWl } from "../../src/indicators/countryRating.mjs"`, when it is called, then `assert.strictEqual` gives a number

AC-10 [P0] — a pair outside the examples gets a wrong WL, with no workaround: Given every ordered pair (p, c) of the 361 pairs from `RATING_SCALE`, when `countryRatingChangeWl(p, c)` is called, then it returns 1 when `notchChange(p, c) === 1`, 2 when it is `>= 2`, and 0 otherwise. The result is always one of 0, 1, 2 (`typeof "number"`).

AC-11 [P0] — bad input that returns 0 hides a downgrade: Given each `v` in INVALID, when `countryRatingChangeWl(v, "BBB")` or `countryRatingChangeWl("BBB", v)` is called, then it throws `RangeError`. `countryRatingChangeWl()` with no arguments throws `RangeError` too.
